title: Ishta Devata and Retrograde Planets
sub: Complete notes on Jyotish Vidya Ep. 4 by Brajesh Gautam, The Anchor Of Life. How grace, karma and an exalted planet determine your Ishta, plus a first look at retrograde Mercury and Jupiter.
desc: Complete notes on Jyotish Vidya Ep. 4, Ishta Devata and Retrograde Planets by Brajesh Gautam: the karma story that opens the class, becoming your own Ishta, the sign-to-deity table, Mars and marriage, Sun and kidney stones, and a preview of retrograde Mercury and Jupiter, with video timestamps.
points: Whether you find the right doctor, astrologer or partner depends on grace from your Ishta, not chance.
An exalted planet can make you your own Ishta.
When your own planet already sits strong in the right house, you may not need to worship anything outside yourself.
The 9th house sign suggests your starting Ishta.
A simple table maps each sign to a planet and a deity, but lagna, bhava chalit and navamsa can each point somewhere different.
Worshipping a weak planet can backfire.
Puja activates a planet's energy, so activating an already debilitated placement can make things worse, not better.
Mars and marriage are tied through fire.
The wedding pheras ignite a manglik Mars; skip the fire with a court marriage or Anand Karaj and the dosha has nothing to activate.
Mercury and Jupiter retrograde both got a preview.
Retrograde Mercury cannot stay quiet, retrograde Jupiter inflates the ego around age 15 to 16; the full class continues in Ep. 5.
The remedy behind most of this is simply not reacting.
Grace, karma and planetary fixes all point back to the same habit: do not give your body to someone else's provocation.
